## 3. First Comment

We built Fabrica because we kept watching founders and operators become the bottleneck between a brief and a result — and it was happening to us too. We were juggling raw terminal windows with Claude Code, Cursor CLI, and Devin. Work lived across disconnected chats and spreadsheets. Agents had no shared context, couldn't talk to each other, and the moment a run mattered, we had no structured way to inspect diffs, track spend, or stop consequential mistakes before they happened.

Fabrica changes this by providing a unified desktop management platform for your CLI agents — with a Slack-style channel interface instead of raw terminal tabs:

1. **Manages your CLI agents via local terminals:** Fabrica spawns and coordinates Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor, Devin, Hermes, Pi, and more. Your API keys remain direct with your providers — Fabrica never calls LLMs or resells inference.
2. **Slack-style channel interface:** No raw terminal tabs — agents report through dedicated channels in plain language. The UI is event-driven (triggering on task completions, budget thresholds, approval gates) and adapts to your preferences over time.
3. **Agents collaborate, not just execute:** Agents talk in dedicated Slack-like channels to delegate tasks and debate approaches, all while referencing a central **Knowledge Vault** and business roadmap (a local document drop folder that serves as the single source of truth). Smart agents immediately know what and when each one needs to do — users don't orchestrate manually.
4. **Built to build AND run:** Use specialized crews for software engineering (with isolated git worktrees) alongside 24/7 ongoing business operations — customer support triage, ecommerce management, YouTube content pipelines, HR intake, and 400+ SaaS automations via our native **n8n plugin**.
5. **Governed by default:** Consequential actions pause at visual approval gates. Hard budget caps stop runaway spend before it happens, with real-time quota tracking on supported agents.

We're not here to sell magic. Early access means integrations are expanding, and we'll say so plainly. If you're a builder, solo founder, project manager, or operator who wants more throughput without handing over judgment — try Fabrica today and tell us what you think. We'll be in the comments all day!
